newsitem.title: FRANCE: Generale des Eaux set to raise Havas stake.
newsitem.headline: Generale des Eaux set to raise Havas stake.

text.p: Generale des Eaux is expected to announce later on Thursday a deal in which it will raise its stake in Havas to 30 percent and become the main player in the French media sector.

Company officials are keeping silent until a news conference scheduled for 1530 GMT on Thursday. But industry sources and French newspapers have indicated Generale will transfer its 19 percent stake in pay-television broadcaster Canal Plus to Havas, which already has a 21.6 percent stake in that company.

Generale and Havas, which are both having full board meetings on Thursday, issued a statement on Monday confirming news reports that they were having talks about their audiovisual interests, in particular their Canal Plus stakes.

According to industry sources Generale will boost its Havas stake, currently less than five percent, by subscribing to a special capital increase and by buying a 10 percent stake, out of a total of 21.2 percent, from Alcatel Alsthom.
Alcatel has confirmed it was in talks with Generale about selling part of its stake.
Havas has a market capitalisation of some 28 billion francs which would put the price of Alcatel's 10 percent at 2.8 billion ($500 million).
The market capitalisation of Canal Plus, at Wednesday's prices, is also about 28 billion francs while Generale des Eaux is worth 90 billion francs on the share market.

The increased Havas stake in Canal Plus will allow the French company, and indirectly Generale des Eaux, to remain the biggest shareholder in the merged group of Canal Plus and Dutch-based NetHold, controlled by Richemont and MIH.

It will also give Generale des Eaux a strong media "pillar" next to its more traditional activities in water and services as well as its latest addition, the Cegetel telecommunications venture with Mannesmann AG, British Telecom Plc and SBC Communications Inc.
Generale des Eaux already ownes Generale d'Images, a unit which operates cable networks in France and Britain and owns such film studios as Babelsberg in Germany.
Generale des Eaux and Havas recently jointly acquired the SFP studios in France from the state.
The combination of telecommunications services and television will allow Generale to be a strong player in multimedia in France and boost its competitive position towards France Telecom.
Its large stake in Havas will also shield that company from an unwanted takeover by a foreign media giant at a time when the industry is undergoing a global shake-up.

"What we're trying to do is create a French group capable of competing with its world rivals...and which will be lasting, without a shareholder which will change every two years," Generale des Eaux chairman Jean-Marie Messier told the French Senate in a hearing on trade globalisation on Wednesday.
"The real battle is taking place on the international market," he said, adding that any group which could not master content, production and broadcasting would be a fragile one.

For Havas chairman Pierre Dauzier, the increased stake of Generale des Eaux will put more pressure on him to improve profitabilty at the group, which started life as one of Europe's first news agencies.
On the stock market there are rumours Havas may now want to take full control of its Havas Advertising unit, while some dealers wonder whether it will keep its travel activities.
Bank Societe Generale, which has a 5.9 percent stake in Havas and 4.5 percent in Canal Plus, had no comment on reports it may be involved in th reshuffle.
Other Havas shareholders are France Telecom and Audiofina which is controlled by Belgian businessman Albert Frere. ($ = 5.582 French Francs)
